chunks: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Amir narrated to us from his uncle Abdullah ibn Amir, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Harun al-Makfuf, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who said:

O Abu Harun! Indeed, we instruct our children to recite the Tasbih of Fatima (peace be upon her) just as we instruct them to perform salat. So cling to it, for no servant who clings to it becomes wretched.

key_terms.تسبيح فاطمة: Tasbih of Fatima — the dhikr formula of 34 times Allahu Akbar, 33 times Alhamdulillah, 33 times Subhanallah, taught by the Prophet to his daughter Fatima
key_terms.صبيان: Children, young ones — indicating this practice is taught from the earliest age
key_terms.فشقي: Became wretched/miserable — the negation serves as a guarantee of spiritual felicity for those who maintain this practice

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about teaching children the Tasbih of Fatima?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) addresses his companion Abu Harun al-Makfuf (the Blind) and reveals the Ahlulbayt's household practice of teaching children the Tasbih of Fatima alongside mandatory prayer. The Imam elevates the Tasbih of Fatima to the same level of importance as salat in the spiritual formation of children, asserting with absolute certainty that whoever adheres to this practice will never be wretched. This hadith is transmitted through the distinguished chain including Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, one of the most authoritative Shia transmitters.

en.bilal-muhammad: Ja`far b. Muhammad b. Masrur (ra) narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn b. Muhammad b. `Amer narrated to us from his uncle `Abdullah b. `Amer from Muhammad b. Abi `Umayr from Abi Harun al-Makfuf from Abi `Abdillah al-Sadiq (as). He said:
O Aba Harun! Surely, we instruct our children to recite Tasbih Fatima (sa) just as we instruct them to pray. So, cling to it, for no wretched worshiper clings to it.
